**Résumé / abstract :**

> Artificial intelligence (AI) is poised to transform clinical practice, but its adoption coincides with a longstanding decline in bedside medicine. Herein, we argue that reintroducing Oslerian principles into medical training may be essential to ensure that technological progress does not come at the expense of the physician-patient relationship. Throughout, we use the term AI to refer to tools built on algorithms, from risk calculators and predictive models to large language models, that produce predictions, classifications or recommendations. These tools have no agency of their own: they operate only on the data supplied to them, and their implementation depends on how clinicians and institutions design and deploy them.William Osler never saw an algorithm. He died in 1919, a century before "artificial intelligence" entered the clinical vocabulary. And yet no figure in the history of medicine is better equipped to tell us what we are about to lose 1 . Osler's central achievement was a discipline of the mind: the conviction that the practice of medicine must rest on direct observation of the patient and on the relationship between patient and physician. However, assessing competence and workforce readiness presents a significant challenge. Entrustable professional activities (EPAs) offer a promising solution by translating competencies into observable, entrustable tasks. While EPAs have been widely adopted in clinical training, their application in non-clinical educational contexts remains minimal. Guided by Rogers' Diffusion of Innovation theory, this scoping review aims to map the diffusion of EPAs beyond medical education and examine their scalability to non-clinical educational contexts, where real-world practice errors may undermine system integrity, educational outcomes, or public trust. This review will progress through five stages following Arksey and O'Malley's framework. Searches will be conducted across Ovid MEDLINE, CINAHL, Scopus, ERIC, and Google Scholar. > Clinical reasoning is an iterative, context-sensitive phenomenon. Its instruction and assessment require distinct forms of educational design. Existing reviews, consensus guidance, and longitudinal curricula provide substantial content and teaching strategies. Further specification is needed to coordinate conceptual preparation, expert modeling, scaffolded whole-case practice, feedback, adaptive fading, and transfer across learner development. We present CRAFT, a theory-informed instructional design model organized around five functions: Conceptualize and Frame, Reveal and Model Clinical Reasoning, Apply Through Scaffolded Practice, Feedback and Reflect, and Transfer Toward Independence. CRAFT provides a curricular architecture organized around proposed readiness gates, in which the five functions recur in progressively more demanding cycles as knowledge, contextual variation, uncertainty, learner responsibility, and assessment stakes increase while instructional support decreases. This article offers a theoretical account of that question. It characterises values education as a relational practice and specifies three conditions that any occupant of the educator's position must satisfy: answerability, exemplarity and address. It then distinguishes five affordances of GenAI, namely the generation of moral content, the simulation of perspectives, Socratic questioning, feedback on moral reasoning, and a tacit curriculum of machine authority, and analyses the risk internal to each. These risks fall into epistemic, relational, axiological and agentic families and are connected rather than independent. The central argument is that a generative model can be a moral interlocutor but not a values educator: it cannot be answerable for what it says, cannot exemplify a life, and cannot address a particular student. > Weight gain and impaired glucose metabolism are common complications of antipsychotic treatment in schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD). While beneficial in other populations, the efficacy and safety of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) in SSD remain unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating GLP-1 RAs versus placebo in SSD patients treated with antipsychotics. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched until January 2026. Random-effects models were used to pool mean differences (MDs), standardized mean differences (SMDs), and risk ratios (RRs), as appropriate. Seven RCTs including 481 participants were included. Compared with placebo, GLP-1 RAs significantly reduced body weight (MD -6.98 kg; 95% CI -10.53 to -3.43), BMI (MD -2.51 kg/m²; 95% CI -3.51 to -1.51), waist circumference (MD -5.05 cm; 95% CI -6.66 to -3.44), HbA1c (MD -0.32 percentage points; 95% CI -0.38 to -0.26), and fasting blood glucose (MD -0.54 mmol/L; 95% CI -0.83 to -0.25). > Epigenetic aging algorithms are emerging tools for understanding the biological effects of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). A growing body of literature has applied DNA methylation-based epigenetic clocks in people living with HIV (PWH) across the life course, examining epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) in relation to HIV infection, antiretroviral therapy (ART), comorbidities, and clinical biomarkers (e.g., viral load, CD4 T-cell counts). This systematic review (Prospero: CRD420251126874) summarizes and synthesizes the current evidence on epigenetic aging in PWH across the life course and identifies critical knowledge gaps for future research. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Medline through June 26, 2026. The review followed PRISMA guidelines and assessed studies for risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. We created a narrative synthesis of results and performed a random-effects meta-analysis of HorvathAge EAA. Fifty-five studies met the inclusion criteria. More than half (n = 33) examined EAA in PWH compared to an uninfected control population. > Abstract This essay offers an overview of the importance of testing for forming objects of knowledge and decision making since the late nineteenth century, focusing on applications in the health and human sciences. We argue that scientific reductionism and bureaucratic priorities – as well as ideas of fairness, feasibility, and marketability – have shaped the development and institutionalization of standardized tests. Against this background, we zoom in on a key socio-epistemological question that has guided our collection: how do experts, patients and regulatory decision makers know that tests and their data are trustworthy? > Objective The aim of this pilot study was to evaluate the preliminary efficacy and feasibility of integrating Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques combined with Clinical Pilates on pain, symptom severity, and sleep quality in patients with fibromyalgia. Methods Twenty women with fibromyalgia were randomized into Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques+Clinical Pilates (n=11) and Clinical Pilates (n=9) groups. The protocol lasted 6 weeks (3 sessions/week). Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques included rib raising, suboccipital myofascial release, Sternocleidomastoid (SCM) mobilization, diaphragm/mediastinum techniques, and visceral mobilizations. Primary outcomes were the Widespread Pain Index, Symptom Severity Scale, and Pressure Pain Threshold. Sleep was assessed via the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Results Both groups showed significant intra-group improvements (p 0.05). Conclusion Integrating Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques into exercise-based rehabilitation presents promising preliminary evidence for enhancing central sensitization symptoms and sleep quality in fibromyalgia patients, though larger trials are needed.

> Background: While conservative management often improves lumbar disc herniation (LDH) symptoms and promotes spontaneous resorption over time, the clinical value of extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) in accelerating this process remains underexplored. Observation: We present a 36-year-old female with an acute, massive right-sided L5/S1 disc prolapse. Following a staged conservative regimen and the subsequent introduction of ESWT combined with acupuncture. Lastly her radicular pain and numbness almost completely resolved. Evidence suggests that HLC is associated with health behaviors, treatment adherence, patient-provider communication, and rehabilitation outcomes. Individuals with a more internal HLC believe that their health outcomes are largely shaped by their personal actions and behaviors. > Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. Trained on sonographer trajectories, the agent integrates spatial, tactile and visual feedback to navigate discontinuous acoustic windows and acquire standard imaging planes. ### Supporting Allyship in Virtual Collaboration with Artificial Intelligence: A Scenario-Based Study

- **Tags proposés** : Aucun tag proposé

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **ai_anchor** : artificial intelligence

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Recent research has revealed that accessibility in virtual collaboration is not only a technical problem but also depends on allyship: the informal, interpersonal practices through which people support others’ accessibility needs. Yet little research has examined how artificial intelligence (AI) might support allyship in collaborative accessibility contexts. To address this gap, we conducted a study where 18 participants (10 disabled, 8 non-disabled) reflected on four allyship scenarios with novel AI tools. Participants valued AI designs that they anticipated could help teammates express, interpret, and coordinate around access needs by reducing repeated disclosure and making allyship more actionable. At the same time, participants raised concerns when AI acted without consent, misrepresented users’ intentions, or displaced the interpersonal work of allyship. Based on our findings, we introduce allyship-support tools as a class of accessibility technologies, offer design guidelines, and discuss AI in particular as a means of supporting allyship.

> Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the central nervous system characterized by inflammatory lesions, neuroaxonal damage, and progressive neurological dysfunction. Early diagnosis and appropriate treatment are essential for preventing relapses and reducing long-term disability. This article examines modern approaches to the diagnosis and comprehensive management of multiple sclerosis, focusing on clinical manifestations, magnetic resonance imaging, cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers, and disease-modifying therapies. A narrative analysis of published clinical studies and international recommendations was conducted. The findings demonstrate that the integration of neurological examination, advanced neuroimaging, and immunological biomarkers improves diagnostic accuracy, while individualized disease-modifying treatment helps reduce inflammatory disease activity and delay disability progression. Comprehensive rehabilitation and regular neurological monitoring remain important components of long-term patient management.

> Decompression sickness (DCS) is an uncommon but important cause of acute myelopathy that neurologists should recognize in the emergency setting. We report a 43-year-old experienced technical diver who developed acute sensory loss with a thoracic sensory level, gait dysfunction, upper motor neuron signs, and urinary retention after rapid ascent from approximately 90 feet below sea level. Thoracic spine MRI demonstrated longitudinal, posterior-predominant T2/STIR hyperintensity from T3 to T10-11 without pathologic enhancement, supporting spinal cord DCS. He received prompt hyperbaric oxygen therapy using U.S. Navy Treatment Table 6, along with 100% oxygen, horizontal positioning, and intravenous fluid resuscitation, followed by additional hyperbaric treatments for persistent sensory and autonomic symptoms. He improved rapidly, regained independent ambulation, and later returned to high-level physical activity, although intermittent sensory symptoms persisted during follow-up. Concussions result from impact or translated forces to the brain, where a cascade of physiological events occur at cellular level, resulting in altered cerebral functioning. Young athletes in Scotland experience concussive injuries in sport, but there remains limited published primary data to support clinical decision-making. Furthermore, skills and knowledge of healthcare professionals supporting youth sportspersons and their available resources are unknown. The work presented in this thesis explores the management of youth athletes in Scotland. In light of this, this paper explores the discursive construction of professional credibility as central to expert identity on X/Twitter. To this end, NVivo 14 was employed to quantitatively and qualitatively analyse 100 posts from four physiotherapy experts, focusing on the use of stance markers (Hyland, 2005b) and qualitatively annotating patterns of scientific verbalisations. Specifically, the results indicate a strategic of—inclusive or exclusive—self-mentions, positively loaded emotional markers, and lexical technicality, based on users’ respective self-presentations as an accessible knowledge-provider, a committed expert, a branded individual, and a transparent knowledge commentator.

> The ependymal cell layer lining the central canal of the spinal cord forms a key endogenous neural stem cell niche in adult mammals, and enhancing its activity may promote repair following spinal cord injury (SCI). We investigated the independent and combined effects of voluntary free wheel running and PNU-120596 (PNU), a positive allosteric modulator of α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, on functional recovery and endogenous plasticity after chronic thoracic contusion SCI. Four weeks post-injury, female rats received PNU or vehicle, with or without access to running wheels, for six weeks. Free wheel running robustly improved behavioural recovery and sensory function. > Context Complete spinal cord injury (SCI) has traditionally been considered irreversible. However, accumulating evidence suggests that subclinical neural pathways may persist. Multimodal combined neuromodulation targeting brain-spinal-peripheral circuits holds promise to unlock latent neural plasticity, but clinical evidence for its application in patients with clinically complete SCI remains limited. Findings A 53-year-old male with chronic complete T9 SCI (AIS A) received a sequential multimodal neuromodulation protocol consisting of spinal cord electrical stimulation (SCS), brain-computer interface (BCI) training, primary motor cortex intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS), and peripheral magnetic stimulation (pMS) of the bilateral iliopsoas muscles, alongside 12 months of conventional rehabilitation. After one year of intervention, his neurological status improved from AIS A to AIS C (T 9 to T 12 ). The left lower limb motor score increased from 0 to 6, accompanied by the recovery of partial voluntary movement. ### Clinical and Serological Evaluation and Management of Rheumatic Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease

- **Auteurs** : Ophir Vinik
- **Revue** : Canadian Respirology Today
- **Année** : 2026

- **Source** : OpenAlex

- **Lien** : https://doi.org/10.58931/crt.2026.2123

- **Tags proposés** : `#incertitude`, `#raisonnement_clinique`

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **uncertainty** : diagnostic uncertainty
  - **low_priority_clinical_topics** : interstitial lung disease

**Résumé / abstract :**

> In 2011, the American Thoracic Society (ATS) recommended that antibody testing be included in the evaluation of patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) to assess for an underlying connective tissue disease, particularly in cases of lingering diagnostic uncertainty, such as differentiating ILD from idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.¹ Specifically, the ATS endorsed routine testing for antinuclear antibodies (ANA), rheumatoid factor (RF), and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti CCP) antibodies. However, autoantibody testing in isolation is rarely diagnostic and results must be interpreted within a clinical context. Accordingly, the interpretation of autoantibody testing and its implications for the diagnosis and management of rheumatic disease-associated ILD remain central to optimizing care in this patient population. Serology testing is best utilized as an adjunct rather than a standalone diagnostic tool. Over reliance on antibody results without clinical correlation can result in misdiagnosis and inappropriate treatment. It is therefore important to integrate serologic data into the broader diagnostic workup of systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease-associated ILD.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Medical knowledge evolves as clinical guidelines revise recommendations, yet whether large language models (LLMs) faithfully incorporate such changes remains unclear. We introduce ChronoEvo, comprising 1,709 recommendation-level revisions across 12 forms of medical knowledge change, to distinguish recognition of revised guidance from incorporation into clinical recommendations. In the primary model, 90.8% of responses recognized revisions and 80.2% were clinically correct, but only 58.5% fully incorporated guidance, yielding a 32.3-percentage-point recognition-incorporation gap. This dissociation persisted across 14 models and was corroborated by two clinicians' adjudicated assessment of 300 responses, yielding a 40.3-percentage-point gap in the validation sample. Changes in recommendation strength and patient eligibility were associated with retention of outdated guidance. A revision-salience intervention reduced outdated-content retention and improved clinical correctness but did not significantly improve full incorporation. These findings identify faithful incorporation of evolving medical knowledge as a distinct challenge for clinical LLM reliability, even when updated guidelin...

> Introduction: The Canadian Undergraduate Urology Curriculum (CanUUC) is a free, online curriculum that covers important topics in urology for medical students. While multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and flashcards are widely used for medical education, they can be resource-intensive and time-consuming to produce. Therefore, to strengthen the CanUUC with such tools, we developed a customized large language model (LLM)-enabled system to generate MCQs and flashcards from CanUUC material and evaluated the quality of its outputs. Methods: We used OpenAI’s GPT-5 model and refined two system prompts to generate educational materials from two CanUUC topics (benign prostatic hyperplasia and urolithiasis). Six evaluators blinded to items’ origin were involved, and each item received two independent ratings for relevance, correctness, clarity, distractor quality, and suitability for education. Items with a mean score 1 plausible answer. Across all independent ratings, the proportion of top scores (4–5) ranged from 85.5−90.5% across all domains. Methods This single-center cohort study screened consecutive patients admitted with suspected AIS from January 2021 through December 2024. Admission PINRI combined an internally standardized logarithmic C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio, the logarithmic systemic inflammatory response index, and the inverse of the prognostic nutritional index; no transportable clinical threshold was proposed. The primary outcome was 180-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0–2, mRS 3–5, or death. Results Among 278 analyzable patients, 111 (39.9%) achieved mRS 0–2, 114 (41.0%) had mRS 3–5, and 53 (19.1%) died; 167 (60.1%) experienced dependency or death. > Cerebral palsy (CP) is a non-progressive neurodevelopmental disorder in which motor features and their functional impact may change across development. Although longitudinal surveillance and multidisciplinary management are established components of CP care, motor phenotype is often treated as static. This narrative review proposes iterative motor phenotyping as a conceptual framework for repeatedly characterizing spasticity, dystonia, ataxia, hypotonia, and mixed motor features in relation to function, participation, comfort, safety, and child- and family-centered goals. Reassessment may be scheduled during follow-up or triggered by developmental transitions, functional changes, by pain, or by limited or unexpected treatment response. Updated characterization can inform individualized management and may prompt targeted diagnostic evaluation when emerging or atypical features raise concern for an alternative diagnosis. Iterative motor phenotyping is intended to complement, rather than replace longitudinal surveillance, rehabilitation, multidisciplinary care, and diagnostic evaluation. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite major pharmacological advances, a substantial gap persists between guideline recommendations and routine clinical practice, particularly after exacerbations. This narrative review summarizes current evidence supporting personalized pharmacological escalation in COPD, focusing on single-inhaler triple therapy (SITT) and the emergence of biologic therapy. SITT, combining an inhaled corticosteroid, a long-acting β 2 -agonist and a long-acting muscarinic antagonist, is now the preferred inhaled strategy for patients requiring ICS-containing triple therapy. Real-world studies indicate that, compared with multiple-inhaler triple therapy, SITT is associated with better adherence and persistence, lower exacerbation rates and improved clinical outcomes, although observational findings require cautious causal interpretation. In parallel, COPD has entered the era of targeted biologic therapy. > Abstract Purpose of Review Enterocutaneous fistulas (ECFs) are complex and resource-intensive complications in surgical and trauma care. Despite improvements in mortality over the past several decades, ECFs continue to be associated with significant morbidity, prolonged hospitalization, malnutrition, and impaired quality of life. This review examines contemporary principles of ECF management and highlights evolving therapeutic strategies. Recent Findings Modern management has shifted from prolonged bowel rest and exclusive parenteral nutrition toward a multidisciplinary approach emphasizing early source control, physiologic stabilization, and nutritional optimization with increasing focus on enteral rehabilitation when feasible. Adjunctive pharmacologic therapies, fistuloclysis, and advanced wound isolation techniques support stabilization and may improve spontaneous closure rates in select patients. > Stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) is one of the most frequent complications after acute stroke, affecting approximately one in eight stroke patients. Besides prolonged hospitalisation and increased healthcare costs, it is also a major risk factor for mortality and poor functional recovery. The pathophysiology of SAP is driven by two converging processes: impaired local airway defence due to dysphagia as well as reduced airway clearance reflexes, and systemic stroke-induced immunodepression driven by dysfunction of the autonomic nervous system. While post-stroke immunodepression is a major risk factor for SAP, it might limit unwanted autoimmune responses within the brain. Conversely, SAP itself may drive neuroinflammation and contribute to post-stroke cognitive impairment. Despite its clinical importance, high-quality evidence to guide practice on prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of SAP remains scarce and guideline recommendations are mostly based on expert consensus. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Aims This study is aimed at describing the oral manifestations and diagnostic pathway of Cowden syndrome in a young patient, highlighting the role of dental professionals in early detection of PTEN-related disorders. Case presentation A 25-year-old woman presented with long-standing, progressive multifocal oral papillomatous lesions since childhood. Clinical examination revealed macrocephaly and extensive papillomatosis involving the lips, tongue, palate, and buccal mucosa. Histopathological analysis demonstrated verrucous epithelial proliferation with parakeratosis, acanthosis, elongated rete ridges, and low-grade dysplasia. Based on the clinical and histological findings, genetic testing was performed and identified a pathogenic PTEN variant (c.388C>T; p.Arg130Ter), confirming the diagnosis of Cowden syndrome. The patient was subsequently enrolled in a multidisciplinary surveillance program. Conclusion Persistent multifocal oral papillomatosis associated with systemic findings should raise suspicion for Cowden syndrome. Early recognition by dental professionals is essential for prompt diagnosis and timely initiation of risk-adapted surveillance strategies.

Data were collected using the Burnout Assessment Tool for Students (BAT-S) to measure academic burnout and the Mental Health Continuum-Short Form (MHC-SF) to measure mental health. The results indicate that academic burnout is a negative and significant predictor of mental health among Generation Z college students in Medan, with a regression coefficient (B) = -0.204, β = -0.474, t = -10.738, and p<0.001. This article examines the Swedish National Gang Exit Programme as a form of administrative desistance. Drawing on three types of qualitative material, the article shows how desistance is structured through four interconnected practices: eligibility assessments, relocation, intervention and monitoring, and outcome classifications. Through these practices, desistance becomes measurable, documented and governed within hybrid arrangements of policing, welfare administration and marketised service provision. Rather than suspending crime governance, the programme reorganises it through continued classification, conditional inclusion and bureaucratic control. The article contributes to research on gang exit programmes and gang desistance by developing the concept of administrative desistance and showing how exit from criminal gangs isshaped through administrative processes that both enable and constrainindividuals’ exit from organised crime. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Multisensory XR may support informal learning for autistic adults, but sensory-friendly design often emphasizes reducing input. We conducted a mixed-methods, counterbalanced within-subjects study with 20 Chinese autistic adults who evaluated five complete XR configurations presenting the same popular-science content. Comfort differed substantially across the configurations (Friedman chi-square(4) = 46.39, p < .001, Kendall's W = .58). L3 received the lowest mean rating (2.97/5) and was tied for lowest for 16/20 participants, whereas L5 received the highest mean rating (4.43/5) and was tied for highest for 17/20. Participants described the static configurations in terms of clarity and self-pacing, L3 in terms of abruptness, simultaneous demands, insufficient warning, and limited disengagement, and L4/L5 in terms of gradual transitions, opportunities to disengage, and coordinated narrative cues. The study provides a configuration-level account of sensory comfort and identifies participant-described qualities that can inform future controlled studies of multisensory XR.

> Patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) proceeding to pancreaticoduodenectomy rarely have a single nutritional problem. Poor intake may coexist with pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, loss of muscle function, systemic inflammation, and unstable glucose control. Screening tools identify vulnerability, but they do not show which of these processes is most important at a particular point in treatment. This Perspective sets out a domain-guided approach in which screening is followed by an explicit treatment hypothesis. Four overlapping domains are considered: muscle loss and functional decline; pancreatic exocrine insufficiency and impaired digestion; inflammatory and catabolic burden; and glycemic instability with pancreatic endocrine insufficiency. The domains are not new diagnoses and do not replace the Nutrition Care Process. They are a practical way to connect a clinically important finding with a defined action, a responsible clinician, a response measure, an escalation rule, and a reassessment date. > Given changes in the religious landscape and in health care in contemporary Western societies, healthcare chaplains are in need of a new shared and communicable understanding of their specific position and role in healthcare institutions. Developing such an understanding not only calls for more empirical studies into healthcare chaplaincy, but also for theoretical models which help interpret and integrate empirical findings. This paper describes the 'liminality model' of contemporary healthcare chaplaincy, which was developed on the basis of structured discussions of an international expert panel. This conceptual model characterizes healthcare chaplaincy as a practice of 'engaging with liminality'. ### When to Use t Test, ANOVA, ANCOVA, MANOVA, and MANCOVA: A Step-by-Step Guide for Novice Educational Researchers

- **Auteurs** : Emmanuel Nestory Kayuni
- **Revue** : Journal of Research Innovation and Strategies for Education (RISE)
- **Année** : 2026
- **Date de publication** : 2026-10-25
- **Source** : OpenAlex
- **DOI** : 10.70148/rise.v3i6.6
- **PMID** : Non renseigné
- **PMCID** : Non renseigné
- **Lien** : https://doi.org/10.70148/rise.v3i6.6
- **Score** : 0
- **Décision** : **Faible priorité**
- **Tags proposés** : Aucun tag proposé

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - Aucun mot-clé fort détecté

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Selecting an appropriate statistical test remains a challenge for novice educational researchers, particularly when distinguishing among parametric procedures with different requirements and analytical purposes. This paper provides a practical guide for selecting the t-test, ANOVA, ANCOVA, MANOVA, and MANCOVA in quantitative educational research. The guide begins with hypothesis testing and variable classification, followed by normality assessment and consideration of data transformation before selecting the appropriate statistical procedure. Each test is explained according to its purpose, assumptions, research question, types, decision criteria, and interpretation. The paper emphasizes the necessity of choosing statistical tests based on the research hypothesis structure, number of groups, dependent variables, and covariates, rather than by familiarity with statistical software. The guide is designed to assist novice education researchers to make sound statistical choices and improve the validity and interpretability of their quantitative research results.

  - **negative_keywords** : dental
  - **source_penalty** : -5 points : dépôt, préprint ou source non prioritaire

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds the output of large language models in retrieved, verifiable external sources and is increasingly proposed as a way to reduce hallucination in AI tools used for learning. Existing reviews of RAG in healthcare have focused mainly on clinical use cases, and it remains unclear how RAG has been applied and evaluated for educational purposes across the health professions, and to what extent dental education is represented. This scoping review will map the extent, range, and nature of the evidence on RAG-based systems used for the education of health professions students. It follows the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews and will be reported according to PRISMA-ScR. Registration timing: this protocol is registered after the literature search (10 September–20 October 2026) and deduplication but before any title/abstract screening, full-text assessment, or data charting.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Caring for post-stroke patients with neurological disabilities at home requires family caregivers to adapt to long-term care demands. Previous studies have mostly described caregiver burden, needs, and barriers and facilitators of adaptation, while how caregivers interpret and negotiate adaptation over time remains underexplored. This study aimed to explore the meaning of adaptation among family caregivers of post-stroke patients with persistent neurological impairments. This qualitative study used a phenomenological approach to explore the lived experiences of 14 family caregivers selected purposively and interviewed through in-depth semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using Colaizzi’s method. Four themes emerged: rebuilding everyday life around patient dependency, learning caregiving through experience and professional guidance, managing emotional exhaustion and changing family roles, and developing acceptance, confidence, and new meaning in caregiving. Conceptually, adaptation is a non-linear process that integrates practical adjustment, negotiation of family relationships, and meaning-making. > India faces a significant challenge with a large educated but unemployed population, partly due to the historical emphasis on general education over vocational training. This has created a workforce imbalance, with a shortage of skilled labor at lower levels. In response, the government has intensified efforts to vocationalize education through various schemes, including the Additional Skill Acquisition Programme (ASAP) in Kerala. This program aims to equip students with market-relevant skills, addressing the demand for a more technically proficient workforce. This study investigates the attitudes of higher secondary school students in Kerala towards the ASAP initiative. A sample of 450 students from different districts was surveyed using a structured questionnaire to assess their perspectives on the program's effectiveness, benefits, and overall appeal. The findings indicate that students' attitudes towards ASAP vary significantly based on demographic factors such as gender, location, and academic stream. In addition, systemic issues such as overcrowded classrooms, irregular academic calendars, and constrained learning resources further complicate the adjustment process. Rather than viewing student struggles as individual weaknesses, this study situates them within broader structural and administrative realities. Central to this framework is the role of structured support systems within faculties, particularly the involvement of administrative units responsible for public order and information management. > Background: Duty handover is a high-risk point in the continuity of maternity care, and breakdowns in handover communication have been linked to delayed care and avoidable harm. Qualitative evidence from maternity wards in low-resource Sub-Saharan African settings is limited, and to our knowledge no study has examined handover experiences on maternity wards in Hoima District, Uganda. This study explored the experiences and challenges of health workers and administrators regarding duty handover on maternity wards in public health facilities in Hoima District, Uganda. Methods: We conducted a qualitative phenomenological study. Fifteen in-depth interviews with maternity ward health workers and five key informant interviews with administrators were carried out across six public health facilities. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed using a modified Colaizzi seven-step method. Reflexivity and bracketing were addressed through a pre-fieldwork assumptions statement and bracketing interview, a reflexive journal kept throughout data collection, and independent double-coding of a subset of transcripts. With global aging populations, the rising prevalence of these disorders presents a growing public health challenge. Current treatments for DMDs are limited by substantial drug side effects and restricted therapeutic efficacy. Gene therapy has emerged as a promising alternative for addressing these conditions. Nanoparticles are essential for overcoming intracellular and extracellular barriers in nucleic acid delivery. Recent technological advances have led to novel nanomaterials and strategies, which have enabled safer and more efficient gene therapy. This review comprehensively analyzes the role of nanoparticle delivery systems in enabling effective gene-based interventions for major DMDs. > This research examines the support conditions necessary for the successful implementation of Indigenization processes as a strategy for poverty elimination. Conducted in collaboration with End Poverty Edmonton (EPE), a municipal-level nonprofit focused on poverty elimination, the study employed qualitative methods, including surveys, one-on-one interviews, focus groups, and Indigenous approaches such as conversations and sharing circles. Findings indicate that successful Indigenization requires four key conditions: reciprocal relationships, collective advocacy, space for reflection and learning, and time for adaptive and incremental change. These factors emerged as essential for fostering trust, shifting power dynamics, and embedding Indigenous ways of knowing within systems. The research underscores that Indigenization is a collective effort requiring both Indigenous and non-Indigenous collaboration, strategic learning, and sustained commitment to systemic transformation. The findings contribute to broader discussions on decolonization, reconciliation, and policy change in municipal and organizational contexts.

> Since 2014, China has comprehensively implemented the Standardized Residency Training (SRT) program nationwide, and the integration of professional postgraduate education with SRT has operated for over a decade. This narrative review, based on searches of Wanfang Data and PubMed from January 2015 to December 2025, examines the achievements, persistent challenges, and reform options of this integration system. While the system has shortened medical training from six to three years and enriched clinical exposure, a fundamental structural contradiction persists: the dual identity of professional postgraduates as both “students” and “residents” creates an inherent conflict between clinical practice and academic training. Within the fixed three-year period, postgraduates bear the combined burden of 33 months of clinical rotations, coursework, and thesis research, leaving insufficient protected time for scientific research, compounded by misaligned training objectives, welfare inequity, delayed licensure, and elevated mental health burdens. Целью данного исследования является комплексная оценка влияния лесоразведения в зеленых поясах на углеродные пулы в свете национальной и международной литературы. Методология исследования основана на аналитическом обзоре результатов крупнейших мировых проектов Трех Северного лесного пояса в Китае, Великой зеленой стены в Африке и экологических программ в Европе. Основные результаты показывают, что масштабные посадки позволяют аккумулировать значительные объемы углерода в биомассе и почве. Однако реализация таких проектов в аридных и полуаридных регионах может нарушить гидрологический баланс из-за повышенного водопотребления насаждений. Ценность проведенного исследования заключается в обосновании того, что успех зеленых поясов нельзя оценивать исключительно по количеству высаженных сеянцев. > Abstract Intestinal ultrasound (IUS) is increasingly used as a point-of-care tool during routine follow-up care for the assessment and longitudinal monitoring of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Although its clinical advantages are well established, implementation across Canada remains uneven. Implementation in Canada has been shaped by variable training capacity, infrastructure, reimbursement, workflow, and provincial health-system organization. A virtual national roundtable of experts was convened to explore the practical role of IUS in contemporary Canadian IBD care, identify barriers to wider adoption, and define priorities for future implementation. The panel included adult and pediatric gastroenterologists from multiple Canadian provinces from diverse practice environments. The discussion was guided by 3 domains: clinical utility, barriers to implementation, and strategies for national expansion. IUS is positioned to become an increasingly important component of treat-to-target IBD care in Canada, but its equitable and sustainable adoption will require coordinated attention to training, quality, infrastructure, and health-system value.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Individuals with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) often face significant barriers in computing education. In asynchronous learning environments, instructional videos can impose high extraneous cognitive load, often relying on assumptions about sustained attention and working memory that do not align with ADHD neurocognitive profiles. In this work, we evaluate a post-hoc video processing intervention that segments instructional content into single-instruction chunks followed by fixed-length pauses to reduce cognitive load. In a within-participants controlled study with 17 individuals with ADHD and 10 without, we find that the intervention has an equalizing effect. Although it improved performance for all participants, gains were larger for those with ADHD, reducing their errors and hesitations to levels comparable to those of participants without ADHD under the same intervention. These results align with the goals of Universal Design for Learning (UDL), by showing that cognitively-aligned, post-hoc instructional video modifications can reduce performance disparities across diverse neurocognitive profiles.

By asking respondents to choose among options, MFC assessments may reduce response biases common in rating scales, such as social desirability, acquiescence, and faking. However, the quality of MFC scores depends on more than the response format. It also depends on how blocks are assembled, how responses are modeled, and how scores are interpreted. This dissertation examines two issues in MFC assessment. Study 1 investigates how option discrimination and option preference parameters affect block option selection. > Objective To develop a national consensus catalog of essential psychomotor competencies and establish the minimum expected competence levels for graduating medical students across anesthesiology and surgical specialties in Brazil using a modified Delphi process. Methods This national consensus-development study used a two-round modified Delphi process coordinated by the Brazilian Medical Association. Scientific Committees representing anesthesiology and 14 surgical specialty societies developed preliminary specialty-specific catalogs and proposed the expected competence level for each competency. Board-certified specialists evaluated the competency-competence-level combinations using a five-point Likert scale. Consensus was predefined as ≥75% combined agreement. Results A total of 802 specialists participated in the first Delphi round, and 622 completed the second round. The preliminary catalogs comprised 343 competency statements. Of these, 273 (79.6%) achieved consensus, whereas 70 (20.4%) were excluded. During the first Delphi round, participants proposed 103 additional competency statements, of which 90 (87.4%) achieved consensus after evaluation during the second Delphi round....

**Résumé / abstract :**

> The aim of the study was to evaluate students’ satisfaction, self-confidence, and knowledge retention after a Health Simulation on Diabetes Mellitus screening in Primary Health Care. This quantitative, quasi-experimental pre- and post-test study was conducted with nursing students at a public university in the Federal District, Brazil. Initially, 46 students participated, 15 in the experimental group and 31 in the control group; 33 completed the knowledge retention assessment. Satisfaction and self-confidence were assessed in the experimental group after the simulation. Satisfaction (4.92±0.27) and self-confidence (4.83±0.79) scores were high. Knowledge scores increased in the experimental (8.72±1.49 to 9.70±0.48) and control groups (8.29±1.34 to 9.30±1.01). The results suggest that the intervention may be a promising teaching strategy in this context. However, inferential analyses are needed to assess between-group differences and determine whether observed changes may be attributed to the intervention.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMSDs), including osteoarthritis (OA), osteoporosis (OP), intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), and sarcopenia (SP), impose a major burden through pain, structural deterioration, mobility loss, fracture risk, and functional decline. Although these disorders are often grouped as age-related musculoskeletal conditions, they arise from distinct tissue niches and cannot be explained by a single pathogenic mechanism. Macrophages occupy a central position at the interface between degenerative stress and tissue outcome, but their functions extend far beyond a binary M1/M2 polarization model. This Review proposes a disease-niche-adapted framework for macrophage reprogramming in DMSDs. In this framework, macrophages are interpreted according to the pathological tasks they perform within each tissue environment: inflammatory amplification and pain-related synovial crosstalk in OA, osteoimmune remodeling in OP, immune-barrier disruption and macrophage-nucleus pulposus (NP) cell feedback in IVDD, and impaired regenerative support in aging muscle in SP. We discuss how macrophage functional states are shaped by transcriptional and epigenetic regulation,...

While considered separate motor imagery modalities, little is known about their separability. Across two studies, this thesis aimed to examine the extent to which VMI and KMI are separable in novices (lacking prior motor experience of the task) from both a neural and behavioural perspective. Study 1 aimed to test the shared and distinct neural mechanisms recruited during VMI and KMI performance using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). In a single session, participants performed VMI and KMI of a novel gesture sequence task inside an fMRI scanner. Study 1 results showed that VMI and KMI recruit distinct sensory regions: VMI showed greater activation in visual regions, whereas KMI was associated with greater activation in non-visual sensory regions. The localized form predominantly affects the hand, whereas the diffuse form mainly involves large joints; involvement of the flexor hallucis longus tendon sheath is rare. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the principal modality for demonstrating the hemosiderin deposits characteristic of this lesion, although histopathology remains necessary for definitive diagnosis. Surgical resection remains the standard treatment. We report the case of a 24-year-old man with 10 months of right ankle pain, related to a diffuse-type TGCT involving the flexor hallucis longus tendon sheath and adjacent ankle joints. Radiographs initially showed soft-tissue filling of Kager's triangle. Computed tomography arthrography demonstrated synovial thickening but was nonspecific; MRI then revealed the characteristic findings, and histopathology confirmed the diagnosis. This report aims to raise awareness of this rare location and...

**Mots-clés détectés :**

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Background Posterior migration of a mobile-bearing cervical disc replacement (CDR) can be catastrophic. The authors report a single-patient case of catastrophic failure after recent trauma and implant loosening. Observations A 48-year-old woman had received C5-6 and C6-7 Mobi-C CDRs at an outside institution 3 weeks before presentation and had sustained a ground-level fall 8 days before presentation. Outside imaging from after the fall showed implant loosening. After subsequently lifting a laundry basket, the patient developed acute quadriparesis with complete motor and sensory loss below C7. CT demonstrated catastrophic C5-6 and C6-7 hardware failure with posterior migration of the C6-7 polyethylene insert into the canal. Emergency revision C5-7 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion was performed, but she remained American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale grade A at the 1-year follow-up. Lessons Patients with recent trauma and radiographic evidence of loosening, posterior endplate translation, loss of endplate parallelism, or polyethylene core malposition should prompt urgent surgical evaluation and likely revision. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26740.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Background: Cervical spinal cord injury (CSCI) carries a high risk of autonomic disturbances, including neurogenic shock and autonomic dysreflexia (AD). Although AD is classically described in the chronic phase (>6 months post-injury), increasing evidence indicates it may also occur acutely, including during spinal surgery, and may result in severe hemodynamic instability if not promptly recognized and managed. Delayed surgical intervention may predispose to earlier manifestation of AD as spinal reflexes begin to recover. Case Presentation: We report a case of AD in a 45-year-old woman with a C3-T1 spinal cord contusion and C7-T1 spondyloptosis who had a complete spinal cord injury (AIS A, neurological level C4) and underwent decompressive laminectomy and posterior stabilization on the day 8 following trauma. Approximately one hour after surgical incision, during spinal manipulation, the patient developed four recurrent cycles of severe hypertension with bradycardia (up to 180/110 mmHg and 40–50 beats/min), followed by profound hypotension. Management included immediate cessation of surgical stimulation, increased propofol dosing, addition of remifentanil target-controlled infusion...

> Background Postoperative symptomatic epidural hematoma (PSEH) is a rare but potentially devastating complication following thoracic decompression surgery, with an incidence of less than 1%. While isolated PSEH has been well documented, recurrent PSEH,particularly in the thoracic spine which represents an exceptionally rare phenomenon with limited literature available to guide clinical management. Case presentation This is a case of a 64-year-old male patient who underwent thoracic decompression surgery for ossification of the ligamentum flavum and developed recurrent PSEH requiring two hematoma evacuations. > Background: Spinal osteoparasitoses caused by Echinococcus granulosus are rare and diagnostically challenging due to sterile cultures, similarity to bacterial spondylodiscitis, and poor response to antibiotic therapy. This study aimed to present a case of Th12–L1 vertebral body involvement and evaluate the diagnostic pathway and treatment effectiveness. Case presentation: A patient presented with localised back pain without neurological deficit, which contributed to delayed diagnosis. Over five months, progressive vertebral destruction, paravertebral abscess formation, and fistula development occurred despite empirical antibiotic therapy. Serological testing revealed an elevated titre of anti-Echinococcus IgG antibodies, confirming the diagnosis. Albendazole therapy (2 × 400 mg daily) was initiated. Four surgical procedures were performed, including stabilisation, abscess drainage, vacuum-assisted closure therapy, and fistulotomy. Conclusions: Parasitic infection should be considered in spinal lesions with sterile cultures and poor response to antibiotics. Multidisciplinary management is essential for accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.

This technical report describes a reproducible IVRB protocol using methylprednisolone, lidocaine, and labetalol and emphasizes procedural details that may influence treatment delivery. Key elements include obtaining venous access distal to the involved region, selecting tourniquet position and pressure according to the affected extremity, slowly infusing the injectate, and performing deep friction massage while the extremity remains isolated from the systemic circulation. The report also describes staged tourniquet deflation, the use of anesthesia to limit procedure-related pain, an initial series of repeated blocks before judging response, and subsequent adjustment of block frequency according to the duration of pain relief. > A 20-year-old female with asthma, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, mast cell activation syndrome, and complex regional pain syndrome Type 1 (CRPS1) presented for left transfemoral amputation with osseointegration and nerve reconstruction. To limit CRPS1 exacerbation, neuraxial anesthesia with femoral and sciatic blocks was administered for analgesia. Given the reported history of convulsions following ketamine and propofol, sedation with midazolam, dexmedetomidine, and fentanyl was used. On POD 1, fascia iliaca and sciatic blocks were repeated to mitigate postoperative pain. There were no intraoperative or postoperative complications. With limited literature on anesthesia for osseointegration, this novel case highlights individualized planning, in the setting of adverse responses to anesthetic medications and challenging pain management.

Here, using a specially designed behavioral paradigm for backward locomotion in mice, we find that glutamatergic neurons in the caudal pontine reticular nucleus (PRNc) are selectively activated during backward, but not forward, locomotion. Activity increase of these neurons is temporally aligned with backward movement, with its amplitude correlated with speed. In conventional αβ T cells, this kind of integrin-ECM engagement has been shown to drive a defined intracellular mechanotransduction pathway: actin polymerisation, nuclear deformation and YAP translocation that together promote IL-2-dependent activation, independently of the T cell receptor. > BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the Clinical Sensory Testing (CSTs) sensitivity and specificity in detecting somatosensory disorders across different populations. DATABASES AND DATA TREATMENT: A systematic search on Medline (PubMed), Cochrane Library, CINAHL, EMBASE and Scopus was performed until August 2025. Eligible studies assessed CSTs in patients with somatosensory dysfunction by comparing them with any reference standard. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (RoB) using QUADAS-2. Results were synthesised narratively and divided by sensory modality. RESULTS: Twelve studies (N = 4911) were included, covering different conditions (e.g., diabetic peripheral neuropathy, lumbar spinal stenosis, neuropathic pain). CSTs demonstrated moderate to high specificity, particularly in pressure, mechanical, and vibration domains, while sensitivity varied widely by tool and modality. The Semmes-Weinstein Monofilament Test showed 77%-90.7% sensitivity and 63.8%-100% specificity; tuning fork vibration tests ranged from 30% to 96% sensitivity and 45%-99% specificity. Because the broader manual therapy literature is heterogeneous and includes multiple overlapping intervention labels, distinguishing direct evidence for Body Engineering from related evidence is important for maintaining scientific neutrality. Objective: To map and synthesize the available literature concerning the terminology, theoretical foundations, therapeutic approaches, proposed mechanisms, clinical applications, and evidence relevant to Body Engineering Rehabilitation and related manual and movement-based approaches in musculoskeletal rehabilitation. > Although objective imaging markers for rehabilitation assessment are available, lumbar disc herniation (LDH) and lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS) remain two common causes of chronic low back pain (CLBP). Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) is a non-invasive imaging modality that allows estimation of water-molecule anisotropy and assessment of the microstructure of nerve roots and paraspinal muscles. Postoperative monitoring, preoperative prognostic assessment, evaluation of conservative treatment, detection of paraspinal muscle degeneration, and prevention of injuries during military training are examples of DTI applications in the rehabilitation and prevention of lumbar degenerative disease (LDD). There are two aspects of “prevention”: primary prevention, which concerns early warning of training injuries; and secondary prevention, which concerns the quality of rehabilitation to avoid long-term disability. However, in Africa, passive therapies are the dominant intervention. Therefore, this thesis aimed to explore attitudes towards LBP rehabilitation, then assess the feasibility of a culturally adapted CBT-informed protocol. The work presented in this thesis is composed of three phases. Firstly, a scoping review was performed to identify patients’ perceptions about LBP in Africa. Secondly, patients’ and physiotherapists’ beliefs of LBP in Malawi were examined using the Back Pain Attitudes Questionnaire and the Pain Attitudes and Beliefs for Physiotherapy questionnaire; and findings informed the adaptation of a CBT-informed protocol. Lastly, a randomised controlled trial assessing the feasibility of the protocol was conducted against usual physiotherapy management in a hospital outpatient setting in Malawi. > Abstract Cowboy-dance kicking is a rapid, multi-joint lower-limb task that requires coordinated activation of multiple muscles, resulting in complex electromyographic patterns for which low-dimensional muscle-synergy analysis can provide a compact description of the recorded coordination structure. Conventional non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) is widely used for such decomposition, but its solutions can be sensitive to initialization and local convergence, and solutions with similar reconstruction quality may still differ in their internal muscle-loading structure. This study therefore evaluated an anatomy-informed Grey Wolf Optimization-assisted NMF framework (GWO-NMF) designed to refine low-dimensional synergy structure while balancing anatomical guidance against reconstruction fidelity. Surface EMG was recorded from eight muscles of the dominant left kicking limb in 12 sports-dance students during metronome-paced cowboy-dance kicking, with 83 valid trials retained for analysis. > Evoked and induced responses are fundamental neurophysiological readouts in the development and assessment of treatments for disorders with impaired neural function. Distinguishing these responses is essential for interpreting single-trial variability, identifying the determinants of these responses, and enabling real-time probing of cortical responsiveness. However, because of dynamic overlap, separating evoked and induced activity remains unsolved at the single-trial level when instantaneous fluctuations of cortical responsiveness are of interest. We developed the Evoked-Ongoing/Induced Separator (EOIS), a framework for separating event-evoked, ongoing, and event-modulated induced activity from single-trial data. EOIS recovers evoked and ongoing/induced components by leveraging their distinct phase-consistency features in MEG and real-time EEG, enabling subject-agnostic single-trial time-series analysis and attribution of cortical response variability to specific components. By delivering component-resolved time series, EOIS enables biomarker refinement, pharmacodynamic readouts, and closed-loop neuromodulation, facilitating translational deployment across individuals and care se...

These views rest on classifying each patient as having neuropathic pain or not, although patients often report several pains. The same binary label is the usual target of prognostic and biomarker studies that aim to predict life-limiting pain. We tracked up to three of the worst pains per interview from injury to one year in 140 TRACK-SCI participants, using the DN4 interview (DN4i, threshold 3). Within three days of injury, half of all pain areas and three quarters of participants met the threshold, and pain-area prevalence changed little over the year. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Cycling is a popular leisure activity and a sustainable mode of transportation, but various accessibility barriers thwart the inclusion of people who have a mobility disability in this activity. Our work presents their perspectives on cycling and addresses the role that technology plays in this context. Through semi-structured interviews with 15 cyclists who have a mobility disability and use diverse accessible cycles, we concentrated on their lived experience and their current and envisioned use of technology. We applied Reflexive Thematic Analysis and crafted three themes, focusing on (1) disabled people’s heterogenous approaches to accessible cycling, (2) wellbeing and social relationships emerging through accessible cycling, and (3) how technology improves accessible cycling and why it is carefully applied by disabled cyclists. Grounded in these results, we propose design goals, calling for dependability of technology, opportunities to self-manage accessibility, and preservation of the original cycling experience, and we appraise the grand challenges of CyclingHCI in the context of accessibility.

> Adult spinal deformity (ASD) is a complex three-dimensional (3D) condition in which spinal alignment, vertebral morphology, degeneration, muscle function, stiffness, balance, and compensatory movement strategies interact to shape and constrain patient-specific spinal function during activities of daily living. Despite this complexity, clinical assessment and surgical planning still rely predominantly on static radiographic alignment, combined with subjective questionnaires and the experience of the surgeon. Parameters describing static spinal alignment based on radiographic images provide key clinical parameters, but they capture only a small part of the biomechanical function of a patient. Patients with similar radiographic alignment may differ substantially in their spinal mobility, especially within the deformity, hip-spine coordination, motion redistribution, and regions vulnerable to progressive worsening or postoperative complications. As youngstock progress through distinct management development periods (fetal and neonatal, preweaning, and post-weaning), each presents unique exposure risks that require different management strategies to aid in the mitigation of BLV. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Cuff-based blood pressure (BP) measurement is a cornerstone of health assessment, yet its mechanism remains unclear and measurement error remains substantial1. On the basis of membrane theory2,3, we propose that external pressure generated by cuff inflation follows a hyperbolic-cosine-shaped axial distribution along the artery, forming a pressure-peak zone (PPZ) beneath the cuff. By combining this external pressure with intra-arterial pressure, we constructed a mathematical model that systematically predicts site-specific vascular motion and hemodynamic changes during BP measurement. In humans, multimodal experiments integrating vascular imaging and synchronized invasive and noninvasive pressure measurements validated the model. The PPZ organizes distinct proximal and distal hemodynamics during cuff pressurization: at DBP, diastolic arterial collapse begins at the PPZ; near SBP, only weak residual blood flow traverses the PPZ and disappears once cuff pressure exceeds SBP. These transitions generated identifiable oscillogram features for DBP and SBP, precisely localized by wavelet scanning. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Body-weight-supported locomotor training has been studied for three decades, yet its clinical outcomes remain inconsistent. The standard interpretation of this inconsistency is that the right dosage, timing, or patient subgroup has not been found. We propose a different reading: the inconsistency may reflect a conceptual underspecification in how loading is understood. Two interpretations of body-weight support coexist in the literature—loading as task difficulty (unloading makes the task easier) and loading as control strategy (unloading changes which neural circuits can participate in the solution). These two interpretations generate different predictions, imply different training protocols, and have rarely been distinguished empirically. We review evidence from spinal reflex physiology, body-weight-supported treadmill training trials, and developmental motor control, and argue that the strategy interpretation is better supported but has not been directly tested against the difficulty interpretation. Three testable predictions are offered that could distinguish the two. The framework has direct implications for the sequencing of load in rehabilitation and for the interpretation o...

Suzetrigine (Journavx), a first-in-class, non-opioid, selective NaV1.8 sodium channel inhibitor, was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in January 2025 for moderate-to-severe acute pain; its role in chronic pain syndromes such as CAP has not been established. This case series describes two patients with CAP of differing pathophysiology started on suzetrigine as an off-label adjuvant analgesic. An 80-year-old man with radicular pain from metastatic prostate cancer to bone, who had declined opioid therapy, had an Edmonton Symptom Assessment Scale (ESAS) pain score that fell from 4/10 at baseline to 1-2/10 over approximately six months, with benefit first reported after three weeks. A 63-year-old man with severe oxaliplatin-associated chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy on a multidrug regimen had an ESAS pain score that improved from 9/10 to 4/10 over three weeks, during which he self-discontinued duloxetine and substantially reduced his gabapentin and oxycodone use. > Objectives Pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis (PVO) is a severe infection with increasing incidence. We aimed to describe long-term population-based temporal trends in incidence, clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, microbiology, and outcomes. Materials and methods We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study including 1,017 adults with multidisciplinary team-verified PVO diagnosed at a tertiary infectious diseases referral centre in the Region of Southern Denmark between 2009 and 2022. Incidence rates (IRs) per 100,000 person-years (PY) were calculated using regional population data and compared across three calendar periods (2009-2013, 2014-2018, 2019-2022). Temporal changes in clinical characteristics, microbiology, diagnostic strategies, and outcomes were assessed. Results In total, 1,017 patients were included. The crude IR increased from 4.7 per 100,000 PY in 2009-2013 to 11.0 in 2019-2022, with the largest increase among patients aged ≥70 years. Mean age and comorbidity burden rose over time. ### Suprasellar hemangioblastoma during pregnancy: illustrative case.

- **Tags proposés** : Aucun tag proposé

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **negative_keywords** : surgical, tumor

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Background Hemangioblastoma is a benign tumor that typically occurs in the posterior fossa but may be found anywhere along the neuroaxis. Its growth behavior may be difficult to predict, and pregnancy has been discussed as a possible growth-promoting factor. Observations The authors report the case of a rare suprasellar apparently sporadic hemangioblastoma diagnosed during pregnancy. Following the progressive worsening of symptoms, the baby was delivered by cesarean section. The patient was treated with stereotactic radiotherapy, resulting in a marked improvement in symptoms and impressive reduction in tumor size. Lessons High vascularity and solid growth with a tendency for surgical complications appear to be typical of suprasellar hemangioblastoma, as indicated by this and several other reported cases. The importance of nonsurgical treatment strategies, including radiation therapy, is emphasized by this case. Pregnancy is one of the factors that has been investigated as potentially growth promoting. The authors speculate that postpartum hormonal changes may have contributed to tumor shrinkage in their case. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26756.

> Congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG) are a broad group of disorders characterized by deficient glycosylation. CDG are caused by mutations in over 160 different genes regulating distinct steps and types of glycosylation. Despite the diversity of CDG-causing genes, patient phenotypes often overlap, with neurological symptoms present across many CDG. However, models to study conserved mechanisms underlying neurological dysfunction across CDG types are lacking. Therefore, we leveraged CRISPR/Cas9 to knockdown 15 glycosylation genes in zebrafish spanning 7 CDG classes. Through behavioral assays and in vivo imaging, we report changes in mobility, response to stimuli, and neuronal activity in many of our models. To uncover the molecular underpinnings of these phenotypes, we performed bulk-RNA sequencing on our models. We report differential expression in genes related to neurological development and function across all tested CDG classes, which will inform future hypothesis-driven studies defining new molecular targets for therapeutic intervention in CDG.

In addition to studying their emergent behavior, a main focus of the mathematical community has been concentrated on deriving their large-population limit. In particular, the mean-field limit consists of describing the limit system by its population density in the product space of positions and labels. The strategy to derive such limits is often based on a careful combination of methods ranging from analysis of PDEs and stochastic analysis, to kinetic equations and graph theory. > Blind or low vision (BLV) students are less likely to graduate from college, particularly in computing. Prior work documents accessibility challenges in high school and college, but we lack understanding of the transition process that produces this “leaky pipeline.” To address this, we interviewed ten BLV college students about going to college to study computing. We analyzed our data through the lens of life transition, specifically Intersecting Liminality. Our findings reveal that some BLV students face such immense digital accessibility and college acclimation barriers that the only way forward as coders is to take on a “second job” as a blind advocate or drop out of the computing major. We argue that the college transition is a critical point for analysis and technological intervention, and further, that Intersecting Liminality provides a useful lens for HCI scholars to unpack the compounding challenges that prevent some BLV students from completing computing degrees.

> Context Sensory impairment after spinal cord injury (SCI) may complicate herpes zoster (HZ) recognition. Findings A 76-year-old man with complete T4* paraplegia developed pruritus and vesicles in the right T4 dermatome without eruption-site pain. The asterisk denotes adjustment for stroke-related left upper-limb weakness. Empiric intravenous acyclovir preceded dermatology assessment. Contralateral shoulder and hand pain developed the day after eruption and was absent on the final treatment day. Conclusion/clinical relevance Focal pruritus warrants skin examination. When HZ is strongly suspected, timely empiric antiviral therapy should not await specialist assessment. The contralateral pain course was noteworthy, but an HZ-related mechanism remained uncertain.

A secondary model based on VGG, ResNet, and EfficientNet architectures was trained to identify vertebral labeling errors. The pipeline also generates image quality metrics including signal-to-noise ratio, contrast-to-noise ratio, coefficient of joint variation, and entropy focus criterion. External validation was performed using 2737 MRIs from four public datasets, and clinical utility was demonstrated in a longitudinal cohort of 51 patients with multiple sclerosis. The nnU-Net achieved the highest performance (Dice: C1 = 0.85, C2 = 0.89, C3 = 0.89), labeling 95.8% of mislabeled cases from the Spinal Cord Toolbox. > Overt osteitis fibrosa cystica is an uncommon presentation of primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) in young adults.A 29-year-old woman presented with low back pain of one year's duration.Lumbar computed tomography (CT) showed multiple osteolytic lesions, and bone scintigraphy showed a metabolic "superscan".Biochemistry showed the following: parathyroid hormone (PTH) 1807.3 pg/mL, hypercalcemia (3.06 mmol/L), hypophosphatemia, alkaline phosphatase 1489 U/L, and severe vitamin D deficiency.Ultrasound and dualphase sestamibi single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) localized a single left inferior parathyroid lesion.Parathyroidectomy yielded an encapsulated adenoma (~5.9 g) without capsular or vascular invasion.PTH fell to 30.9 pg/mL on day 1 but rose to 310.3 pg/mL by day 64, while calcium remained mildly low (2.03 mmol/L), consistent with compensatory skeletal remineralization and vitamin D deficiency rather than proven residual disease.A neuropsychiatric event at 13 months was of uncertain relationship to PHPT.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Knowledge Tracing (KT) has become a central approach for modeling students' evolving knowledge states, but conventional sequence-based KT models offer limited representation of relationships among skills, concepts, and assessment indicators, reducing their interpretability for monitoring mastery and learning progression. This study systematically reviews how graph-based and knowledge graph-enhanced KT models have been developed, integrated, and evaluated to support skill mastery, learning outcome monitoring, and assessment-related interpretation. A PRISMA-based Systematic Literature Review was conducted using Scopus and IEEE Xplore, covering publications indexed from 2015 to 2025. From 116 initial records, 20 studies satisfied the eligibility criteria for active graph-enhanced KT and were included in the synthesis corpus, comprising 8 core (40.0%) and 12 supporting (60.0%) studies. Six major integration families were identified, including GCN/GNN-based, Knowledge Graph/ontology-enhanced, heterogeneous or multiplex graph, attention-over-graph, Q-matrix/concept map-based KT, and graph-supported recommendation. > STUDY OBJECTIVES: Actigraphy sleep-wake classification methods increasingly seek to leverage raw acceleration data and machine-learning-based classification, but performance evaluation in pediatrics is limited. We trained machine-learning models using pediatric data and compared their sleep-wake classification performance with existing algorithms for children. METHODS: Sixty-five children (46% female, ages 5.3-17.7 years) completed in-lab overnight polysomnography and wore a GENEActiv device on their non-dominant wrist. The acceleration data were converted into 30-second epochs and aligned with physician-scored sleep-wake data from electroencephalography. Eight machine-learning models were trained using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. Epoch-by-epoch analyses generated performance metrics (e.g., balanced accuracy [BA]) and discrepancy analyses provided overall sleep duration bias estimates. The combination of highest performance and least bias was used to rank using Euclidean distance scores - where a lower score represents closer to perfect performance and zero bias. > Objective: to investigate whether resting-state EEG aperiodic parameters (i.e., offset and exponent) are associated with symptom burden and demographic factors in patients with persistent post-concussive symptoms (PPCS) and differ from healthy controls. Methods: In this cross-sectional observational study, resting-state eye-closed high-density EEG was recorded in patients with PPCS and in age-matched healthy controls. Aperiodic parameters were extracted from EEG power spectra. In patients, hierarchical multiple linear regression models included age and sex as a base model, with additional demographic and clinical symptoms entered separately. Patient-control differences were assessed using multiple linear regression adjusted for age and sex. Results: Seventy patients with PPCS (54 female; 39.57 ±12.21 y.; 109.5 [76.5; 196] days post-concussion) recruited from a concussion care pathway and 38 healthy controls (17 female; 39.61± 13.57 y.) were included. In patients, younger age and male sex were associated with higher offset and exponent values (all p under .014). **Résumé / abstract :**

> Purpose of review Shoulder instability in pediatric and adolescent athletes is increasingly common and clinically complex due to early sport specialization and high-demand participation. This review aims to inform clinical decision-making by synthesizing contemporary evidence on injury patterns, diagnostic techniques, treatment options, and associated outcomes when faced with treating pediatric athletes. Recent findings Unique anatomic and developmental features specific to the pediatric population including capsular elasticity, collagen composition, open physes, and evolving glenoid and humeral morphology contribute to age-specific injury patterns and influence treatment outcomes. Younger children more frequently sustain atypical soft-tissue lesions, while adolescents experience markedly higher recurrence risk with rates of 44-77% following nonoperative management. Adolescents also develop off-track Hill-Sachs lesions more frequently than adults (24.4% vs. 3.3%), reflecting differences in immature bone mechanics. > Background Head and neck cancers (HNC) comprise 5% of all malignancies worldwide. Cetuximab is the first targeted therapy to demonstrate a significant survival benefit in patients with locally advanced HNC (LAHNC) and recurrent or metastatic HNC (R/MHNC). In view of this, we undertook this economic evaluation to ascertain the costs and health benefits associated with (i) the use of RT + CTX over RT alone for LAHNC patients who are ineligible for cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy and (ii) CT + CTX over CT alone for R/MHNC patients from the perspective of Indian healthcare system. Methods A Markov model was constructed to assess the lifetime costs and health outcomes using cetuximab in combination with radiotherapy (RT + CTX) for treatment of cisplatin-ineligible LAHNC ( Analysis I ), and cetuximab in combination with platinum-based chemotherapy (CT + CTX) for treatment of R/MHNC patients in India ( Analysis II ). **Résumé / abstract :**

> Neuropathic pain (NP) is not merely simple persistent pain but a complex pathological condition mediated by dysregulation across multiple systems, including the neuro-immune-endocrine axis. As a high-intensity endogenous stressor, persistent pain signals can deplete cognitive resources and trigger neuroinflammation and central sensitization, leading to cognitive impairment (CI) characterized by attention deficits and impaired working memory. Currently, mainstream pharmacological treatments for NP carry risks of addiction and may exacerbate CI. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop synergistic intervention strategies that address both pain management and cognitive protection. Given that NP and CI share multiple pathological pathways, identifying interventions capable of simultaneously targeting multiple mechanisms has become a research hotspot. Vitamin D, a secosteroid hormone with both neuroprotective and immunoregulatory functions, is closely associated with an increased risk of NP and CI when deficient. > This chapter examines on-demand learning in health as part of broader lifelong learning strategies aimed at strengthening public health systems in the Global South. Moving beyond purely technological interpretations, it argues that technology-mediated lifelong learning should be understood within the institutional, political, and territorial realities that shape health workforce development and public service capacity. Grounded in lifelong learning studies and critical perspectives on the Global South, the chapter develops a theory-informed comparative analysis of four large-scale digital learning initiatives operating at regional, national, and global levels: the PAHO Virtual Campus for Public Health, the Brazilian AVASUS platform, OpenWHO, and the WHO Academy. Through a qualitative and document-based approach, the analysis explores challenges related to workforce shortages, territorial inequalities, scalability, multilingual access, and institutional coordination. The chapter suggests that the effectiveness of on-demand learning depends not only on technological innovation, but also on governance capacity, public policy alignment, and institutional integration.
